utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Could we have the case called, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we proceed I just want to make sure that the two accused are able to follow what is now being said in a language they understand. Mr. Milan Lukic? THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Sredoje Lukic. THE ACCUSED S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. That seems to be in order. Could we have the representation. Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution Dermot Groome and I'm accompanied by Verica Balikic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And for Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, I am Bojan Sulejic and I'm the lead counsel representing Milan Lukic and with me, to my greatest pleasure, is my colleague from Albuquerque, Jason Alarid who was appointed as my co-counsel a few days ago, and together with us is our case manager, Jelena Rasic. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sulejic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm Djuro Cepic, counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic appearing with me is Mr. Jens Dieckmann is the co-counsel, and Christina -- Ms. Christina Kerll is our assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Well, the same line-up for you as last time. For those who have joined respective teams, welcome to the case. We have quite a few items on the agenda and I know that they have been comprehensively and skillfully dealt with during the 65 ter Conference which was chaired by Ms. Yvonne Featherstone yesterday so I think most of the things would be well-digested and maybe we have also had some progression on some fields which were unclear yesterday. So I would like to start with the question of the alibi issue, if I could term it like that. There are some motions which are pending and the first on my list is the Prosecution's motion to preclude the notice of alibi regarding Milan Lukic because it was filed too late. Is that correct, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I noticed that it was filed after we filed that application so I would withdraw the application to prohibit it, but it is the Prosecution's position that what was filed does not comply with Rule 67.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: That is understood. It means that your motion is hereby then dismissed. And we then have the -- in the respect that it seeks an order for preclusion of the evidence of alibi is dismissed in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I'm not withdrawing the application itself that what was filed was insufficient, which we filed after they filed their 67 notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I understand but you're no longer seeking an order that they should not be able to bring evidence on alibi in the case or that Mr. Lukic should not be able to do that. That's the position; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: With respect to that first application, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: In that respect your motion is then dismissed. I have understood that the issue of the substance, if you will, of the notices are also linked to various issues where there is a need to interview, I believe, from the Prosecution the need to have an interview with the accused, both of them, and also I understand that there is a need to -- from the part of the accused to have access to Prosecution witnesses. I see all these issues as interlinked, and I would like to hear where we are on this, and I again turn to you, Mr. Groome. What is it more that you seek in order to have a firm position on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to the notice that was served, it's the Prosecution's position that it is deficient, more deficient in the case of Milan Lukic than Sredoje Lukic. In the case of Milan Lukic there are -- much of the Rule 67 notice are simply claims that he was not present. In some cases he refers to large numbers of unnamed witnesses without addresses, so it's really -- the Prosecution is unable to proceed with the investigations that it must undertake to explore this alibi. With respect to Sredoje Lukic, the Prosecution was just asking confirmation statements, we were provided with statements that spoke about addresses that these people lived at the time that they witnessed what they with -- they witnessed of their observations with respect to the alibi. The Prosecution was seeking to confirm, are those still the current addresses where we might be able to seek information about those people and then the Prosecution was also seeking to establish are there any documents or any other evidence upon which the Defence of Sredoje Lukic is going to rely on for alibis, so in the event forensic testing is required that we would have an opportunity to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sulejic, comments?

utterances.speaker: MR. SULEJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, I have to inform you about a major step forward that has been done in the defence of Mr. Lukic. This is also part of my submission that I sent to the Prosecution when I was on my own in the team. Since my appointment I have managed to design the whole concept of my client's defence which my predecessors failed to do for over a year. I completely agree with the Prosecution that the text according to Rule 67 that we submitted is not enough for the Prosecution to investigate the defence. However, at this moment since my learned friend Jason Alarid is with me today and I have spent a lot of time with him discussing the whole idea of the defence and our appearance, I would kindly ask you to allow him to address you on the issue because I believe that he has more experience with the type of law that is practised here at the Tribunal and he's more familiar to this type of procedure than I am. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sulejic. I'm certainly not going to deny Mr. Alarid the opportunity to address, but I want to know if you need more time to move this along or what the problem is because you see, Mr. Sulejic, we're not going to decide on the substance today, I just want to know what time frame you're in. And also in respect to what I understand the request to have your client being interviewed by the Prosecutor but if you don't feel you're ready to respond to this, I'm certainly happy to listen to your co-counsel. If he's ready. He seems to be ready.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please so we can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would -- I would like to address the alibi information because we've been working hard with Mr. Lukic. I've been to four meetings at this point with him and at this point in time we've received four names of which we would be prepared to give to the Prosecutor, but we also would like a little extra time in just doing our own due diligence. We have a duty to the Court in terms of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: How long do you need? Sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Alarid, how long do you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would ask for 30 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I'm prepared to give you 14 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Fourteen days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: So 28th of March. And I take it then all issues related to this, including your final position as to the interviews and have them carried out within that time as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Judge. I mean, I believe that we need to do a little due diligence as to the names given to us and we believe that we'll be able to have more. So we don't want to give it piecemeal per se. We'd like to have as much possible for the Prosecutor to follow up on and then follow up with an interview with our client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. For Sredoje Lukic, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think we fully comply with the Rule 67 in our motion in relation to alibi defence, and just to give a clarification, we gave more than it's necessary, more than it's complied with. We gave the witness statements in both languages, in B/C/S, in English, and also just for clarification, we -- in that motion we filed current addresses of mentioned witnesses. And I already informed in relation to the town of Obrenovac where those witnesses live. So I gave additional information to Mr. Groome by e-mail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Groome, are you happy with these comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I am very appreciative to Mr. Cepic for that information. The only other outstanding matter with respect to Sredoje Lukic and the question is, is the Sredoje Lukic going to rely on any documents or any kind of physical evidence that -- if so, we would seek to inspect it. If it's not in their possession, we would seek to know where it is so we can inspect it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Are you ready to address that now, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, our obligation is under the Rule 67 as soon as we find something or collect something to disclose to OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I would urge you to look into the matter with the concern to what the Prosecution said and the same time frame would then apply to you in order to move this issue forward. So the 28th of March to have the parties come to a conclusion on those matters regarding the alibi and then obviously the -- if there are any outstanding issues the Chamber will decide on it. So a report is sent to obviously to the senior legal officers not later than the 28th of March to see where we are on this matter. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Nods from the Defence on both sides confirms this. Thank you. I think we then could move to other pending matters which are the Rules 92 bis and ter motions. And just to see that I have understood it correctly, the motion was filed on the 15th of February by the Prosecution. Response was due on the 29th of the same month. No response yet filed by the Defence for Milan Lukic. Mr. Sredoje Lukic Defence timely filed his response on the 28th. And then in addition to that the Prosecution has sought leave to reply in motions filed on the 5th and 6th of March. So it seems when it comes to Mr. Sredoje Lukic matters are ready for a decision but for Milan Lukic we haven't heard anything. Comments? Mr. Sulejic or is it again Mr. Alarid who wants to address?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I understand that you may be seeking to switch positions so you would be the lead counsel and Mr. Sulejic the co-counsel, is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That was at the request of both the client but more importantly, Judge, it's based on a mutual agreement between counsel. We've kind of creating -- we definitely needed to amend the work plan as it was otherwise submitted. I understand the deadlines that are passed, coming up, and also the Trial Chamber's desire to get this moving, and so in to kind of efficiently deal with those time constraints, we're really trying to comply with the Court's needs and organise our team in such a fashion. 16

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: So I understand. You take the paperwork and put that in motion in order to have that settled then with the registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We will do that, Judge, and we also anticipate filing either a motion for additional funding and/or a change in complexity. They're kind of related and we look at them in the alternative of each other, really. The client actually doesn't like the idea of the increased complexity level but in order for us to comply with a -- a -- what we believe is a fast-approaching trial date, there's a lot of work to get covered including some things that we probably should have had done beforehand just to respond to these motions. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And where are you now on the 92 bis and ter motions?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm just in the infancy, Judge. Your Honour, we -- well, basically I'm in the process of beginning to read the Vasiljevic transcripts. I think that's important to put in context the request for using priorly adjudicated materials and all we were given from a Mr. Jatman [phoen] was 11 disks with very little attorney work product on them. It's mostly disclosure material and, of course, that has to be cross-referenced to the Vasiljevic trial in order to determine what relevance was used. One --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I take it that you intend to respond to this then?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: There hasn't been an indication to as to why you didn't respond within the time set.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think it was just a lack of familiarity of the team with the materials they were requesting be included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: So that is the reason why you now seek an extension. How much would you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would like the original 60 days that counsel was allowed to review the entire disclosures, since we are reviewing the disclosures from scratch this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Alarid, this is not going to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: We are not restarting this trial. I understand that you have had problems with the change of counsel, I am obviously aware of that. And for that reason and that reason alone, I'm minded to grant you an extension to respond to the 92 bis and 90 ter motions, but it will not be longer than 14 days. So also here you are obliged to respond to that within 14 days, i.e., the 28th of March. Let me also -- thank you, Mr. Alarid. Let me also indicate that at this point because you what you raised, Mr. Alarid, I think it's time to air this already now, it is clear that we have some fixed timetables and those are set for the very reason that this case should be brought to trial as quickly as possible. Now, we also know the way scheduling of trials happen in this Tribunal, that nothing is yet set in stone. It means that the Trial Chamber is obviously not yet assigned and whether this will happen after Easter and at what time I'm not familiar with the scheduling process. Nothing has to me indicated that the times we have laid down should not hold, and that's what I and also you then should be guided by. When it comes to certain of these motions they would be dealt with by the pre-trial Chamber, but some of them are better left for the Trial Chamber to hear the case, and that would, according to the practice we have in the Tribunal, be, for instance, for the matters of 92 bis and ter and related matters and also goes, I should indicate, the point we will come to, namely the issue of adjudicated facts. But that does not mean that we will hold the time lines for a proper preparation of that indefinitely or in abeyance, and that's why the time lines are as short as they are in this motion, because we know that all of a sudden even if there is a change in -- in plans when this case should go to trial, and I appreciate that both counsel for Mr. Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic are aware that it is in the interest of their clients that this case is brought to trial sooner rather than later. It means that if changes happen, it can also happen the other way that all of a sudden this is put on the back-burner but all of a sudden it's on the front-burner again, because for some reasons that we cannot control. So we should not be -- even if now after Easter there is an indication that this case may not be brought to trial before summer, I'm not saying this is going to happen I'm just trying to share with you my anticipation, it could very well change again. And that's a fact of life that counsel will have to live with, and it is shared equally, this burden, with the Prosecution and with the Defence teams. So now I've shared with you the anticipation of how things is going to evolve and that means that we need to focus. And I appreciate the concern that you have, Mr. Alarid, which you shared, but you need to then exert whatever extra energies you have in order to -- to do your end as it were, and I'm not going to hold you or the team against you that you may have lapsed in the past, but there is no reason now for lapse in the future. I think that is by the nodding that that is understood. Thank you. So we then come to a special part of the 92 bis which is -- has to do with experts and I understand there is an issue there whether there was timely disclosed under 92 bis as well. Would the Prosecution like to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, some of the experts that the Prosecution -- there are a couple of issues with the experts. The experts that testified in the Vasiljevic case, it's the Prosecution's intent to not only use their expert reports from the Vasiljevic case but also to rely on their testimony. I don't believe, especially in light of the alibi evidence, that it doesn't seem that one of the issues at trial will be whether there were people killed or where the bodies were recovered from, so it's the Prosecution's position that the motion was appropriately made under 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And again here we are obviously at the same time line for response in this matter from Mr. Milan Lukic. I would say -- Defence for Mr. Sredoje Lukic, you may be the objection that the clock, as you put it, should not start to run. And I can give you my response it is. It has started to run, and that means that the -- the comments that you should make should timely be made from both of you, then, the 18th of March on this, and that may be a bit soon for both of you. I'm minded to extend that to the 28th of March. I understand from the Prosecution there was an indication at the 65 ter that you wanted to -- to add another expert; is that correct Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the alibi that's been imperfectly raised by Milan Lukic suggests that he was involved in military activities outside the vicinity of Visegrad. When we do receive the information about where he precisely was, if it seems that during the course it maybe helpful to the Trial Chamber to have information about what military activity was taking place in the vicinity of Visegrad, we would be seeking at that time to -- as soon as we get the alibi notice, to review whether we have documentary evidence that our military analyst would be able to testify about and at that time we'd make a decision whether or not to apply for an additional expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, in light of the -- my ambition to have these matters clarified by the 28th of March, how soon thereafter would you be able to disclose whatever additional military expertise you need to -- to bring to the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, as soon as I get some information about where and what operations and have some information in the filing from Defence, I can task the military analyst to work on it promptly as soon as I have the information about where Mr. Lukic says. Now if the Defence can make a representation here today that the information provided in that original filing is the only information about the military operation, I will speak to the analyst after we leave here today and I would -- and could commit to having a report or some indication of whether we would file a report within the next week or two, have him review the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I would appreciate that if you then report on that matter also on the 28th of March and no later than.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. Well, that would bring me, unless the parties need to address any other matters on this, to the Rule -- Rule 94 motions on adjudicated facts. And again we have filings from the Prosecution where responses are due on the 13th of March, and we have a response from Mr. Sredoje Lukic but nothing from Milan Lukic for reasons that are now well-known. We also have notices of proposed agreed facts both regarding Milan Lukic and Sredoje Lukic from the Prosecution. Do the parties wish to address this matter as well? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the Court will entertain an oral application for an extension for leave -- for us to file a leave to reply. As you know, we are filing all of our 65 ter submissions and pre-trial brief this Friday and it will also be impossible for us to also reply by this Friday. If the Court would be so kind as to grant us an additional week, we would like to reply to the response of the Sredoje Lukic team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that would be in order. You are hereby then granted leave to reply to the response not later than 21st of March. Was that noted, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And of course the time that Mr. -- Defence for Milan Lukic will have, I think, should be then properly adjusted to what we have said before, namely the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: May I speak, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think just as a housekeeping matter in the extensions of which the Prosecution would like because of our late tendering would be under the assumption that the Prosecution would get the same benefit of our extensions in terms of filing responses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Maybe they don't want to seek a leave to reply to your response, if that is what you're after.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: We take it when it comes. Or do you anticipate that you need to reply to that response as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I appreciate the generosity but we will not need additional time to reply. As soon as we have it, we can meet our deadlines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: That's what I thought. Thank you. Let me also say when it comes to agreed facts in relation to what the Defence for Sredoje Lukic indicated in its response, which was filed on the 10th of March, that I see the agreed facts as a matter linked to adjudicated facts in the sense that if you have adjudicated facts which are not opposed, they are technically to be treated as agreed facts. And agreed facts is something that the parties obviously are at liberty to deal with throughout the case. I wouldn't say an ultimate limit for it but it goes without saying that the more the parties can agree on facts or consent to adjudicated facts the better it is for everyone. So we will not close the door on any discussions which the parties wish to entertain on the matters of agreed facts and adjudicated facts. And I'm also very much aware that this also is linked to the question of alibi because it could, were the Prosecution to recognise the validity of alibis offered, I would imagine it would impact on the indictment as such. Isn't that true, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It would, Your Honour. And if the Court reviews the history of Mitar Vasiljevic, he served alibi notice and after being interviewed by the Prosecution several weeks after that, the Prosecution actually dismissed several of the most significant counts against him. So that is why we're very anxious to investigate this and do a thorough job and we take our responsibility to investigate it quite seriously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome. And that of course by extension would mean that the pleas that have now been entered by the accused could also change depending on the reactions from the Prosecution and I certainly would encourage all sides to work in that atmosphere to try to see what could be reduced and if that entails a change of plea, the better. On my list I also have a late filing from Mr. Sredoje Lukic. It's a confidential filing so I think we shouldn't give too much as far as specificity here on this. It's a Rule 54 bis motion, and it was filed as early as the 7th of November, 2006, and this will engage then another state presupposes steps to be taken. And I just want to inquire, Mr. Cepic, whether the motion as it lays is enough to act or whether you feel the need to refile it and then update it with whatever steps you may have taken already since the filing in November 2006. Do you have any comments on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We just collected -- we marked everything what we collected. In meantime, we didn't find anything else in relation to mentioned material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: No, I understand that you haven't found anything as far as disclosed by the Prosecution, but have you acted in any other way in order to get the information you seek from this state?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: As is -- as is attached in the annexes of the motion we tried with authorities of the Bosnia and Herzegovina and also before that with relevant broadcasting companies but the answer was no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I understand that, but I just want to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: After that, nothing has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: So I take it then we will then take this and we will issue a decision in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Let me then look at the disclosure matters as they stand. The Prosecution pre-trial brief is due, as Mr. Groome indicated, very soon, on the 14th of March, this Friday. And that will then entail obviously the witness and exhibit lists. I hesitate here because I had an indication, Mr. Groome, that you wanted to -- to add witnesses which are yet not disclosed to the Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The preparation of the pre-trial brief there are witnesses that some for the substantive charges and some for the alibi so we will be filing our witness summaries this Friday, and shortly thereafter we'll be completing disclosure, 66(A)(ii) disclosure on those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: And what is the reason for your inability to disclose them already now?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just -- they've just been selected in the last few days, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I take it you are not anticipating or wishing for this to be disclosed after you filed your pre-trial brief. Is that what you're seeking?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Within a week after the filing of the pre-trial brief after we've made a final selection of our witnesses we would be disclosing the information or the statements that we require to under the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Yeah. I'm a bit puzzled about this, because I would -- to me it would seem given the length of preparations that have been available to the Prosecution that it wouldn't be any need to disclose anything after the filing of the pre-trial brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I've just returned to the office after being aware for some time so I'm not sure of the history but I do know that we have not completed all of our disclosure. I can create a report for the Chamber if the Chamber wishes with more detailed information about the history of when different disclosures were made and when different witnesses were identified as being relevant to the trial in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: There is no need, Mr. Groome, to make a lengthy report, but if you are, as you seek, to indicate to disclose a week after the submission of the pre-trial brief, I think there is a need for some reasoning in the pre-trial brief for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I will include that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. When it comes to disclosure in general it seems to me that the supporting material to the indictment, i.e., Rule 66(A)(i) seems to have been disclosed in total. Is that correct, Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: When it then comes to (ii), the witness statements you anticipate to have apart from a few which you will seek to disclose later including in the pre-trial brief; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you indicate how many statements we are talking about? How many? Just give us a -- just give us a figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In total we've disclosed 54 statements. 34 of those are under 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I stand corrected, 42 have been disclosed under 66(A)(ii).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That is noted. And when it comes to 66(B) i.e., the inspection by the parties to material, photos and the like, is that ongoing or is there a need to set times for this as well? Mr. Cepic, you want to address us?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that we will have a good cooperation with Mr. Groome. I already sent him one e-mail with request for some material but before that just with your leave to underline something which we already requested Mr. Groome and I discussed yesterday and also Defence of Mr. Milan Lukic. In relation to the interview of Milan Lukic which he gave to OTP, I think that this interview has to be delivered to our Defence and this material is under the Rule 66(A)(i).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, on this, Mr. Cepic there could be some disagreement. I understand that this is something that the co-defendant has in party to his counsel which has now come to the possession of the Prosecution, and I suggest if the -- if this cannot be resolved by the parties, and I haven't yet heard Mr. Groome on this, I think, Mr. Cepic you need to move in writing for this material to be disclosed. What is your position on this Mr. Groome?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document that Mr. Cepic is talking about is, I think, about a five-or six-page letter provided to my predecessor by the former Defence attorney for Mr. Milan Lukic. The first paragraph sets out that it's given under certain conditions. The Office of the Prosecutor gave undertakings with respect to those conditions. One of them is that we are prevented from providing it to anyone else. I provided the Milan Lukic team yesterday with a copy of it so that they could review it. And if they consent, then the problem is solved; but if not, as Your Honour has pointed out, it may be a matter that needs to be brought before the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid, are you in position now to indicate your position on this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honour. We've consulted with the client last night on the specific request of disclosure and we would be objecting to its disclosure pursuant to the original terms of the agreement, more so it also would violate Mr. -- the attorney of becoming a witness because this was not a direct statement with recordings and all the other safeguards for authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. Well, it seems, Mr. Cepic, if you want to pursue this matter, you need to move in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Further, when it comes to Rule 68 exculpatory material that is obviously an obligation which is ongoing. Are there any problems or matters that needs to be raised on that? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Just to say -- to say on the record what I've said to Defence counsel, since this is an alibi case I'm suggesting and offering the services of the Office of the Prosecutor to develop search terms which can be most useful to them in searching the large quantity of materials we have in our possession, but it really requires some assistance or some participation by the Defence in process to identify the material that's most useful to their alibi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Will the parties be able to indicate a time that they would need before the 28th of March to try to come to an agreement with the Prosecution on the search terms, which seems to be a sensible way to move forward on this? If not, I would suggest that you try to reach an agreement with the Prosecution before the 28th of March on this as well, so that we don't slip on this. Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With your leave, we would like to see the whole collection of OTP and maybe to select something what is -- what could be useful for our defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Well, that's part of the discussion you will take with -- with the Prosecution on this. I'm not going to rule on this but I would suggest that the parties try to come to an understanding. If that is practical or whatever, it's for the Prosecution then to assist you on this because this is an onus that is on the Prosecution, but it is as the Prosecution points out, in light of the alibi now offered it's a special requirement that needs some fine-tuning and that is what the Prosecution offers. So I think you need to engage in the dialogue and let's say that you report back then, Prosecution and the Defence for both counsel, to the senior legal officer not later than the 28th of March and where we are on this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand when it comes now to the scope of the length of the trial that we have some open matters obviously, I mean, we touched upon the Defence alibi. We've touched upon the 92 bis, ter statements related matters. So I understand Mr. Groome that this is not an easy task if I ask you if you can estimate the length of trial but give me a maximum minimum. I mean, if you indicate that you were to be granted all your wishes as far as 92 bis is concerned, what would be the estimated length of the trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it's possible for me to defer that statement until Friday, we're in the process of really trying with great precision making our 65 ter submission to work out in very -- with great precision what the time would be so by Friday I would be able to give you rather specific numbers. I'd be -- I'd be hazarding a guess if I were to talk off the top of my head at this moment, though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: I look forward to the filing on the 14th of March. We have touched upon that time in the work plan looking at other dates in the work plan just to remind ourselves after the pre-trial brief, the Defence pre-trial briefs are then due six weeks later, i.e., the 25th of April. And the early indication of a Pre-Trial Conference by 16th of May, 2008, still stands with the caveat that I earlier indicated that things after Easter and May evolve in such a way that the present scheduling for this case may have changed but we will, then, obviously let the parties know if there is a change in that. So for this time and this moment these times are valid. Are there any other matters that the parties when it comes to the work plan and the matters we have dealt with need to raise any issue or we have overlooked an issue that you feel that we need to address again? Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Defence for Mr. Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise. Your Honour, what we would be addressing but of course we'll do it first through the registry and I'm sure there will be some consulting that will happen is we'll be making requests for adjustment based on the exceptional, legal and factual circumstances that have arisen through how this case has evolved. Some of it may be self-inflicted by the previous circumstances of the case but definitely we would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Alarid. Are you saying that you are will come back and then seek leave to change the times that we have laid down?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I will do my level best to honour the Court's requests. I think that's important because you need to see that we're working.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And this will show that we're working. But I think from a grand scheme approach, definitely we would be in an ineffective assistance of counsel position were circumstances to remain the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You put that on record now. Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I now turn then to the two accused. As you know you have an opportunity if you want to address the Court in a matter that deals with your personal well-being, and I don't know whether the matters you have indicated, Mr. Milan Lukic, that you want to address. Is this something we can do in open court or do we need to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please. THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] We can deal with this in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Mr. Milan Lukic. THE ACCUSED M. LUKIC: [Interpretation] I heard something from Mr. Cepic according to which I gave an interview to the Prosecution. He referred to some sort of an audio recording. I can claim with full responsibility, and bring Mr. Harmon here if you like, but all I will admit is my own handwriting. I never gave any audio recordings because people in the detention unit say that I had something recorded, I reported on something. They're threatening my family too. I don't know what is at stake but if there are any audio recordings, provide them to Mr. Cepic. I don't know what -- what we're dealing with here. I only wrote down something. They -- they set up the affair in Visegrad. They killed my brother. They wanted to kill me. I didn't give any interviews of any kind. I'm saying this quite frankly. When the time comes for me to give an interview, the public will know the truth. I won't lie, but no one can prevent me from telling the truth. I'm prepared to be held to account for anything I did, but not for what I haven't done. I don't know what sort of CDs we are talking about. That's the truth, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. I'm sure counsel will take note of what you have now put on the record. Thank you. Mr. Sredoje Lukic, do you need to or do you want to address the Court on anything?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please. THE ACCUSED S. LUKIC: [Interpretation] There is nothing I would like to say. Everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE THELIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Well, it seems then that we have come to an end of this Status Conference. As we all know, the need to have a 65 ter Conference before the Pre-Trial Conference may arise and in that case the senior legal officer will inform you of it, and if there is any change to that date as well, as I have indicated -- but as I said before, I at present do not see any change so that is what we all should be guided by. And with that this Status Conference is adjourned. Thank you.
